title: Korean War Begins: DPRK Invades South Korea
note: June 25, 1950 invasion confirmed. Seoul fell June 28 (three days), consistent with claim.

title: Korean War Armistice Signed at Panmunjom
note: Signed July 27, 1953. DMZ established roughly along 38th parallel. No formal peace treaty — all facts confirmed.

title: Kim Il-sung Consolidates Absolute Power
note: Post-armistice purges of Soviet and domestic factions confirmed. Foundation for hereditary rule confirmed.

title: Juche Self-Reliance Ideology Introduced
note: Speech delivered December 28, 1955 confirmed. Some scholars argue Juche as formal ideology dates to 1965, but the 1955 speech origin is consensus.

title: August Faction Incident: Failed Coup Against Kim Il-sung
note: 1956 party plenum coup attempt by Soviet and Yanan factions confirmed. Subsequent purges confirmed.

title: Songbun Political Classification System Formalized
note: Developed between 1957-1960, Politburo adopted May 30, 1957. Event year 1960 is the upper bound of the formalization period — acceptable.

title: Mutual Defense Treaties with Soviet Union and China
note: USSR treaty July 6, China treaty July 11, 1961 — both confirmed. Dual alliance playing Moscow vs Beijing confirmed.

title: Byungjin Parallel Development Policy Announced
note: December 1962 KWP Central Committee meeting confirmed. Cuban Missile Crisis context confirmed.

title: DMZ Conflict Escalates: Second Korean War
note: Conflict ran October 1966 to October 1969; total killed 75 US + 299 SK + 397 NK. Description says 'over 100 US and South Korean soldiers' — actual confirmed figure is ~374 US+SK combined. Minor overstatement but same order of magnitude. Blue House raid Jan 1968 and Pueblo Jan 1968 confirmed.

title: July 4th Inter-Korean Joint Communique
note: Issued July 4, 1972. Three principles (independence, peaceful means, national unity) confirmed.

title: Socialist Constitution Adopted, Kim Il-sung Becomes President
note: Adopted December 27, 1972. Kim Il-sung assumed presidency. Juche elevated to constitutional ideology. All facts confirmed.

title: Kim Jong-il Secretly Designated as Heir
note: February 1974 8th Plenum of 5th Central Committee confirmed. OGD control confirmed. Not publicly disclosed until 1980 confirmed.

title: Invasion Tunnels Discovered Beneath the DMZ
note: First tunnel discovered November 15, 1974 confirmed. Subsequent tunnels in 1975, 1978, 1990 confirmed.

title: Axe Murder Incident at Panmunjom
note: August 18, 1976. Two US Army officers (Captain Bonifas and Lt Barrett) killed. Operation Paul Bunyan response confirmed. North Korea issued unusual statement — not 'formal apology' but 'regret' per sources, consistent with description.

title: North Korea Defaults on $770 Million in Western Loans
note: Default began mid-1974/1975; $770M figure is plausible ($730M overdue by end 1977 per CIA data). The event description assigns year 1976 — consistent with the period when default was formally recognized. Minor discrepancy in exact figure but within range of contemporaneous estimates.

title: Japan Abductions Program Begins
note: Abductions confirmed from 1977. Megumi Yokota abducted November 1977. Official Japanese government count is 17, not 13. Minor discrepancy — event says '13 officially acknowledged' but correct figure is 17. Noted but not material enough for FALSE.

title: Kim Jong-il Publicly Designated Successor at Party Congress
note: Sixth KWP Congress October 10-14, 1980 confirmed. Elected to Politburo, Secretariat, and Military Commission confirmed. First open hereditary succession in communist state confirmed.

title: Rangoon Bombing Kills Four South Korean Ministers
note: October 9, 1983 confirmed. 21 killed (not stated in title — title says 'four South Korean ministers' which matches confirmed death toll of 4 senior cabinet ministers). Total deaths 21. Two agents captured (not just two captured); one killed — confirmed. Burma severed relations confirmed.

title: North Korea Signs the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty
note: Acceded to NPT December 1985 under Soviet pressure confirmed. Delayed safeguards agreement (7 years) confirmed.

title: KAL Flight 858 Bombing Kills 115
note: Confirmed 115 killed is incorrect — actual death toll was 104 passengers + 11 crew = 115 total. Wait — re-check: Wikipedia states 104 passengers and 11 crew = 115. The event says '115 people aboard' which matches. VERIFIED on death toll. However the event says 'Agent Kim Hyun-hee was captured and confessed' — her actual name is Kim Hyon-hui (same person, alternate romanization). Also, the crash location: event says 'Andaman Sea' which Wikipedia confirms. Reclassifying as VERIFIED — the 115 figure is correct.

title: KAL Flight 858 Bombing Kills 115
note: November 29, 1987 confirmed. 115 total aboard confirmed (104 passengers + 11 crew). Andaman Sea crash confirmed. Kim Hyon-hui captured and confessed confirmed. Intended to disrupt 1988 Seoul Olympics confirmed.

title: Both Koreas Admitted to the United Nations
note: September 17, 1991 admission confirmed. Four-decade impasse ending confirmed.

title: Soviet Collapse Triggers Severe DPRK Economic Crisis
note: Soviet dissolution December 1991 and termination of subsidies confirmed. GDP contraction through 1990s confirmed.

title: Joint Declaration on Denuclearization of Korean Peninsula
note: Signed December 31, 1991 confirmed. Commitments not to test, produce, or possess nuclear weapons confirmed.

title: IAEA Inspections Reveal Undeclared Plutonium Activities
note: 1992 IAEA inspections at Yongbyon revealing discrepancies confirmed. NPT withdrawal announcement March 1993 confirmed.

title: First Nuclear Crisis: DPRK Announces NPT Withdrawal
note: March 12, 1993 NPT withdrawal announcement confirmed. Clinton administration military strike consideration confirmed. Jimmy Carter diplomacy and Agreed Framework confirmed.

title: US-DPRK Agreed Framework Freezes Nuclear Program
note: October 21, 1994 signing confirmed. Plutonium freeze for heavy fuel oil and LWRs confirmed. Collapsed in 2002 over HEU program confirmed.

title: Kim Il-sung Dies; Kim Jong-il Assumes Power
note: July 8, 1994. Age 82 confirmed. Heart attack confirmed. Eternal President designation confirmed.

title: Catastrophic Famine — The Arduous March
note: Famine began 1995-1996 triggered by flooding confirmed. Death estimates 240,000 to 3.5 million confirmed. International humanitarian assistance accepted confirmed. Informal market growth confirmed.

title: North Korean Submarine Grounds Off South Korean Coast
note: The submarine was a Sang-O class (not Shark class as stated). 25 infiltrators aboard (not 26). Of the 25: 11 shot by own side, 13 killed in firefights, 1 captured — total 24 dead/1 captured (not '24 killed and one captured' as stated — 24 is correct but the breakdown differs). The class identification 'Shark-class' is materially wrong; it was a Sang-O class submarine.

title: Mass Defection Wave Through China Begins
note: Large-scale defections via Tumen River during famine confirmed. China classifying crossers as economic migrants confirmed. South Korea defector community growing to over 30,000 confirmed.

title: Taepodong Missile Launched Over Japan
note: August 31, 1998 launch confirmed. Overflight of Japan confirmed. No confirmed satellite in orbit confirmed. Japan imposed sanctions confirmed.

title: Revised Constitution Establishes Military-First Governance
note: September 5, 1998 constitutional revision confirmed. National Defense Commission elevated to highest organ of state confirmed. Songun military-first policy codified confirmed.

title: First Inter-Korean Summit in Pyongyang
note: June 13-15, 2000 confirmed. June 15 Joint Declaration confirmed. Nobel Peace Prize for Kim Dae-jung confirmed. Kaesong and Kumgang tourism projects confirmed.

title: HEU Program Disclosed; Agreed Framework Collapses
note: October 2002 HEU confrontation confirmed. Agreed Framework collapse by December 2002 confirmed.

title: Koizumi-Kim Pyongyang Summit; Abduction Admission
note: September 17, 2002 summit confirmed. Kim Jong-il's abduction admission confirmed. Pyongyang Declaration confirmed.

title: DPRK Withdraws from NPT; Six-Party Talks Launched
note: January 10, 2003 NPT withdrawal confirmed. Six-Party Talks launched August 2003 confirmed. First country ever to withdraw from NPT confirmed.

title: Six-Party Talks September 19 Joint Statement
note: September 19, 2005 Joint Statement confirmed. Banco Delta Asia $24 million sanctions confirmed. Agreement collapse confirmed.

title: First North Korean Nuclear Test
note: October 9, 2006 confirmed. Yield under 1 kiloton confirmed. UN Resolution 1718 confirmed.

title: February 13 Agreement Temporarily Shuts Yongbyon
note: February 13, 2007 agreement confirmed. Yongbyon shut and IAEA monitors confirmed. 50,000 tons HFO confirmed. Monitors expelled 2009 confirmed.

title: Second Inter-Korean Summit Produces October 4 Declaration
note: Roh Moo-hyun Pyongyang visit October 2007 confirmed. October 4 Declaration confirmed. Lee Myung-bak government stepping back confirmed. Last summit until 2018 confirmed.

title: Second Nuclear Test; Withdrawal from Six-Party Talks
note: May 25, 2009 confirmed. Yield 2-6 kilotons confirmed. UN Resolution 1874 confirmed. Complete Six-Party withdrawal confirmed.

title: ROKS Cheonan Sunk by North Korean Torpedo
note: March 26, 2010 confirmed. 46 crew killed confirmed. International investigation torpedo finding confirmed. South Korea sanctions and end of inter-Korean trade outside Kaesong confirmed.

title: Yeonpyeong Island Artillery Bombardment
note: November 23, 2010 confirmed. Two South Korean marines and two civilians killed confirmed. South Korea changed rules of engagement confirmed.

title: Modern Uranium Enrichment Facility Revealed at Yongbyon
note: Siegfried Hecker visit November 2010 confirmed. ~2,000 centrifuges confirmed. Transformed international understanding confirmed.

title: Kim Jong-il Dies; Kim Jong-un Succeeds
note: December 17, 2011 confirmed. Death on private train confirmed. Kim Jong-un succession confirmed. First third-generation dynastic succession in communist state confirmed.

title: Third Nuclear Test Claims Miniaturized Device
note: February 12, 2013 confirmed. Yield 6-16 kilotons confirmed (various estimates 7.7-12 kt). Miniaturization claim confirmed. UN Resolution 2094 confirmed.

title: Jang Song-thaek Publicly Executed
note: December 12, 2013 execution confirmed. Uncle by marriage confirmed. Treason and corruption charges confirmed.

title: UN Commission of Inquiry Documents Crimes Against Humanity
note: February 2014 report confirmed. Crimes against humanity finding confirmed. ICC referral recommendation confirmed. North Korea denial confirmed.

title: Sony Pictures Cyberattack by Lazarus Group
note: November 2014 hack confirmed. FBI North Korea attribution confirmed. Lazarus Group confirmed. Threats against theaters confirmed.

title: Kaesong Industrial Complex Permanently Closed
note: February 10, 2016 closure announced confirmed. Response to 4th nuclear test and satellite launch confirmed. $120 million annual hard currency confirmed. South Korean workers expelled and assets seized confirmed.

title: Fourth and Fifth Nuclear Tests — Claimed Hydrogen Bomb
note: 4th test January 6, 2016 confirmed. 5th test September 9, 2016 confirmed. Yield 4th: ~6-9 kt (hydrogen bomb claim disputed by experts). 5th: 17-30 kt confirmed. Resolutions 2270 and 2321 confirmed.

title: Cryptocurrency Theft Operations Target Global Exchanges
note: Lazarus Group crypto theft from 2016 onwards confirmed. Estimated $3 billion by early 2020s confirmed (now over $6 billion total). Adaptation to financial isolation framing confirmed.

title: Assassination of Kim Jong-nam with VX Nerve Agent
note: February 13, 2017 at Kuala Lumpur airport confirmed. VX nerve agent confirmed. Two women as delivery mechanism confirmed. Malaysia expelled North Korea's ambassador confirmed.

title: ICBM Tests Demonstrate US Mainland Range
note: Two Hwasong-14 tests July 2017 confirmed. Hwasong-15 November 2017 covering entire US mainland confirmed. Combined with 6th nuclear test September 2017 confirmed.

title: Sixth Nuclear Test — Thermonuclear Hydrogen Bomb
note: September 3, 2017 confirmed. Event states 100-160 kt yield; later estimates suggest 250-400 kt — minor discrepancy, early estimates were 100-160 kt which is what was widely reported at the time. Thermonuclear claim confirmed by analysts. UN Resolution 2375 confirmed.

title: Three Inter-Korean Summits and Panmunjom Declaration
note: Three 2018 summits confirmed (April 27, May 26, September). Panmunjom Declaration April 27 confirmed. Kim first NK leader on South Korean soil confirmed. September Military Agreement confirmed.

title: Trump-Kim Singapore Summit — First US-DPRK Leaders' Meeting
note: June 12, 2018 Singapore summit confirmed. Joint statement with denuclearization commitment confirmed. Limited substantive progress confirmed.

title: Nuclear Testing Moratorium Declared; Punggye-ri Site Closed
note: April 2018 moratorium announcement confirmed. May 24-25, 2018 Punggye-ri demolition confirmed. Not a binding commitment confirmed.

title: Hanoi Summit Collapses; Diplomacy Frozen
note: February 27-28, 2019 collapse confirmed. Trump refused Kim's Yongbyon-for-sanctions offer confirmed. Year-end deadline confirmed.

title: North Korea Seals Borders Due to COVID-19
note: January 22, 2020 border closure confirmed. Trade with China collapsed confirmed. Denial of COVID-19 cases for over two years confirmed.

title: Inter-Korean Liaison Office Demolished
note: June 16, 2020 demolition confirmed. Protest over leaflet campaign confirmed. Communication lines severed confirmed. Established 2018 confirmed.

title: Party Congress Admits Economic Failures; New Weapons Goals Set
note: January 2021 8th Party Congress confirmed. Kim admitted five-year plan 'fell short in almost every category' confirmed. New weapons goals (tactical nukes, multi-warhead missiles, hypersonic, SLBM) confirmed.

title: Record 90 Missile Launches; ICBM Moratorium Broken
note: Record 2022 launch count confirmed (~90). Hwasong-17 ICBM full-range test confirmed (March 2022 claimed by NK; South Korea disputed; November 2022 unambiguous). Moratorium broken confirmed. China/Russia blocking UNSC action confirmed.

title: Nuclear Doctrine Law Codifies First-Use Posture
note: September 8, 2022 law confirmed. 'Irreversible' nuclear state confirmed. First-use scenarios confirmed. Delegation of launch authority confirmed.

title: Kim-Putin Summit: North Korean Weapons for Russia-Ukraine War
note: September 2023 summit at Vostochny Cosmodrome confirmed. Artillery/missiles for satellite technology exchange confirmed. South Korea and NATO condemnation confirmed.

title: First Military Reconnaissance Satellite Successfully Launched
note: November 21, 2023 launch confirmed. Third attempt (first two failed) confirmed. Russian technical assistance credited confirmed. South Korea suspended 2018 Military Agreement confirmed.

title: DPRK Declares South Korea Principal Enemy; Abandons Reunification
note: January 2024 Supreme People's Assembly session confirmed. 'Principal enemy' declaration confirmed. Arch of Reunification demolished January 19-23, 2024 confirmed. Reunification organizations dissolved confirmed.

title: North Korean Troops Deployed to Russia for Combat
note: October 2024 deployment confirmed. 10,000-12,000 troops estimate confirmed. First DPRK combat deployment outside peninsula since 1970s confirmed. Advanced military technology in exchange confirmed.

title: Constitutional Amendment Permanently Enshrines Nuclear Status
note: October 2024 constitutional amendment confirmed. Removal of denuclearization language confirmed. South Korea as primary enemy codified confirmed.

title: North Korea-Russia Mutual Defense Treaty Ratified
note: Treaty signed June 18, 2024. Ratified by Russia November 9, North Korea November 11, 2024. Into force December 2024. Event dated 2025 is slightly off — ratification occurred November 2024. Year should be 2024, not 2025.
year_flag: Year listed as 2025 but ratification was November 2024. Should be 2024.
